reader: GC owner, CFO or project executive deciding how the company should manage contractor COIs as the subcontractor count grows
questions: Is it better to manage subcontractor COIs in a spreadsheet, outsource COI tracking, or use software?
When does a COI tracking spreadsheet stop working for a general contractor?
notes: Buyer's guide ramp item 4 (P10). Vendor-neutral: names no vendors, so no vendor screenshots. Links our COI Journal report spreadsheet-service-software in the body (not under sources). Competing pages are all vendor pitches; none weighs all three models against per-project requirements and endorsements, and none says when a spreadsheet is the right answer. The one thing none has: the three models compared on the two checks that catch gaps (project requirements and endorsement wording), plus who makes the final call in each, and a hybrid path.
